questions.question: What is the primary purpose of major case management in CSM?

options.text: To handle cases from major customers only
To manage communication and resolution for issues affecting multiple customers
To escalate cases to senior management
To track major system outages in IT

explanation.correct: Major case management handles issues that impact multiple customers. It enables coordinated communication and resolution processes when a single issue affects a large customer base.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Major cases are about impact scope, not customer importance level
Escalation is separate from major case management
System outages are tracked in ITSM, not CSM major case management

source.excerpt: Configure major issue management to manage the communication and resolution process for issues that impact multiple customers.

questions.question: What is the relationship between a case and an interaction in CSM?

options.text: Cases and interactions are the same record
An interaction captures the communication channel, while a case tracks the issue resolution
Cases automatically create interactions when closed
Interactions replace cases in the latest CSM version

explanation.correct: Interactions capture the omnichannel communication (email, chat, phone) with customers, while cases track the actual service issue and its resolution. One interaction can lead to creating a case for issue resolution.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Interactions and cases are separate records with different purposes
Interactions typically precede or accompany cases, not follow them
Both interactions and cases are used together in current CSM

questions.question: What are case tasks used for in CSM?

options.text: To replace the main case record
To break down case work into manageable pieces that can be assigned to different people
To automatically close cases after a time period
To schedule recurring customer follow-ups

explanation.correct: Case tasks break down the work required to resolve a case into smaller, manageable pieces. Different tasks can be assigned to different team members, enabling parallel work on complex cases.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Case tasks are child records of the case, not replacements
Case closure is handled through state transitions, not tasks
Scheduled follow-ups are different from case tasks

questions.question: When should case escalation be used in CSM?

options.text: To automatically route all new cases to managers
When a case requires attention from higher-level support or management due to complexity or customer impact
To transfer cases between agents in the same team
To close cases that have been open too long

explanation.correct: Case escalation is used when a case requires attention from higher-level support or management. This typically occurs due to complexity, SLA risk, customer impact, or when standard resolution approaches are insufficient.

wrongAnswers.explanation: New cases go through normal routing, not automatic escalation
Team-level transfers are reassignments, not escalations
Old cases may trigger escalation but not automatic closure

questions.question: What is a case digest in CSM?

options.text: A summary email sent to customers about their open cases
A condensed view of case information and activity for review
A method to merge duplicate cases
A security feature for case data encryption

explanation.correct: A case digest provides a condensed view of case information and activity, making it easier for managers and reviewers to quickly understand case status and history without reading all details.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Customer communications are separate from case digests
Case merging is a different feature from digests
Case digest is about summarization, not security

questions.question: How does a parent-child case relationship work in CSM major case management?

options.text: Parent cases are always higher priority than child cases
A parent case represents the major issue while child cases track individual customer impacts
Child cases must be resolved before parent cases can be created
Parent and child cases cannot have different assigned agents

explanation.correct: In major case management, the parent case represents the overarching issue affecting multiple customers, while child cases are linked to track each individual customer's impact and resolution status.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Priority is independent of the parent-child relationship
Parent cases are created first to identify the major issue
Parent and child cases can have different agents assigned

questions.question: What is the CSM Configurable Workspace?

options.text: A customer-facing portal for self-service
An agent interface optimized for handling customer service cases and interactions
A configuration tool for system administrators
A mobile application for field agents

explanation.correct: The CSM Configurable Workspace is an agent interface specifically designed for handling customer service cases and interactions. It provides a unified view of customer information, case details, and tools needed for efficient case resolution.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Customer-facing portals are separate from the agent workspace
System administration is done through different ServiceNow interfaces
Mobile apps for field agents are part of Field Service Management

questions.question: What happens when a case moves through its state flow in CSM?

options.text: Nothing changes except the state field value
Different actions, validations, and notifications may be triggered based on state transitions
Cases automatically resolve after reaching a certain state
State changes are only cosmetic and don't affect case behavior

explanation.correct: Case state transitions can trigger different actions, field validations, notifications, and workflow steps. The state flow controls the case lifecycle and what happens at each stage of resolution.

wrongAnswers.explanation: State changes often trigger business rules and workflows
Cases don't automatically resolve; agents must take action
State changes have significant behavioral impacts

questions.question: A software company experiences a bug affecting 500 customers. How should they manage this in CSM?

options.text: Create 500 separate unrelated cases
Create a major case for the bug and link child cases for affected customers
Wait until all customers report the issue before creating any cases
Create one case and add all 500 customers to it

explanation.correct: Major case management should be used for issues affecting multiple customers. Create a parent major case to track the overall bug resolution, with child cases linked for individual customer impacts and communications.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Unrelated cases make coordinated resolution difficult
Proactive case creation is better than reactive waiting
One case for 500 customers loses individual tracking capability

questions.question: What are case actions in CSM?

options.text: Automated scripts that run on case creation
Configurable buttons and options that allow agents to perform common operations on cases
Keyboard shortcuts for case navigation
AI recommendations for case resolution

explanation.correct: Case actions are configurable buttons and options that allow agents to perform common operations on cases. They streamline agent workflows by providing quick access to frequently needed actions.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Automated scripts are business rules, not case actions
Keyboard shortcuts are different from case actions
AI recommendations are part of Now Assist, not case actions
